short: Clinics report on paper, and municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2025).
gaps: No row names the tiers using the system, and no count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published; the one source says facilities report on paper, undated beyond its June 2025 publication. The strategic plan is in preparation and not reported as adopted, and the 2024 domestic allocation (AGO-010) is not tied to the system by name.

short: Health centres enter their own reports into the national reporting system (2023), but no figure shows how many of them do.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of health centres keying their own reports: the newest fact on the point (BDI-007, mid-2022) publishes none, and disagrees with BDI-027 (2020), which reads 'all health centres enter their data themselves' as 100% with no numerator, denominator or date, and with BDI-016 (2019), which says 'the majority' without a figure. Nothing on clinics is dated inside the last three years; the community flag rests on one UNICEF stock application described as interfaced with DHIS2 and still in test in 2023.

short: Health zone offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system in 2022; how many clinics enter their own is not published.
gaps: No number or share of primary clinics keying their own reports is published: the 2022 yearbook says only that certain equipped facilities and community relays do (BEN-017, against BEN-016 the same year), and the one count held is a single named private clinic in Cotonou (BEN-006), which does not carry the country. Tiers rest on 2019 and digitisation on 2022, nothing below the health centre is named, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to the as-at; the domestic budget line is for the directorate's information systems and does not name SNIGS or DHIS2.

short: Clinics and hospitals reported into the national system in 2024, entered at district or facility; the share of clinics entering their own is not published.
gaps: No source gives a number or share of primary clinics, or of districts, keying their own monthly reports; the facts disagree on where data is digitised, the newest (BFA-007, 2025-01) saying facility entry is being scaled up while the 2024 yearbook (BFA-022) still gives district keying from paper as the general route and facility entry only in the districts implementing it. Finance is not stated, and no row shows a community system exchanging data with Endos-BF: community reports reach it on paper through the CSPS and the district (BFA-041).

short: All public health facilities reported into the national system in 2016-18; they report on paper (2025), and it is unclear where the figures are entered.
gaps: No admitted source names the level at which facilities' paper reports are keyed: BWA-002 establishes only that entry is not at the facility, and the one row saying district (BWA-003) is from the excluded source. The 100% figure (BWA-025, 2018) counts facilities reporting through DHIS2, not clinics entering their own data, and has no numerator or denominator; tiers and that share are dated 2018-19. Inside the 36 months no plan or finance fact is held, and nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: The national reporting system runs in all 35 districts (2025), but only 21.4% of 14 facilities checked in 2024 entered data electronically.
gaps: No fact says primary clinics enter their own reports: the 21.4% is 3 of 14 hospitals and health centres chosen for access and security in Bangui and three regions (to July 2024), not a national share, and the only tiers fact is from 2020. The plan and the donor finance are dated 2020 and 2022, outside the 36 months, and the completeness rise to 2025 is a year-dated trend, not an event placed inside the twelve months; CAF-004 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: In 2020 departmental health offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system; nothing more recent shows where reports are entered.
gaps: Every coverage fact dates from 2020 to 2022 and nothing later says where clinics' reports are keyed. The 2021 plan has DHIS 2 deployed in a few first-contact establishments (CIV-025) without saying they enter their own reports, so T3 is not held and the 2020 statement that none do stands. No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months, no dated event inside the twelve, and the community flag rests on the platform publisher's own statement in systems.csv.

short: The national system is in use countrywide with entry at the facility (2022 ministry plan), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so.
gaps: No source gives a count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 96% completeness for October to December 2025 measures reports received in DHIS2, not who keyed them. Where data is digitised is in dispute: the ministry's April 2022 plan says facility entry (the newest dated fact, and nothing on tiers or entry point is dated since), while its 2020 plan and WHO's SCORE (2018 data) put entry at district, and the 2022 plan still budgets a device per facility at 20% of users a year. Tiers are not broken down by level in any source. A DHIS2-based community system was designed and piloted in 2022, with no row showing it exchanging data with the HMIS, so community integrated is not set.

short: Health zone offices enter facilities' paper reports into the national system (2021), which covers 75.3% of all health facilities (2022).
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after 2022. The 75.3% (12,050 of 16,010 facilities, 2022) is the share of all facilities whose monthly reports are in DHIS2, not of clinics keying their own, and the source does not say who keys them; no share or count of facilities entering their own reports is published. The tiers value is from Sud-Kivu alone (COD-026), and the national table of 2020 (COD-032) names only health centres and referral hospitals. No plan dated inside the 36 months is held: PNDIS II ended in 2024. The advancing event (COD-005) is an HIV analysis dashboard inside the national DHIS2 made the primary tool in one province, not a change in where data is entered.

short: All 52 health districts enter clinics' paper reports into the national system (2024); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
gaps: No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and the PNDS says facilities report on paper; health posts (T4) are not mentioned and general hospitals (T1) were configured but not yet reporting. The 401 data collectors equipped for electronic transmission are dated only to 2025, with no tier, denominator or software named, so it is not established that the event falls inside the twelve months or that it is facility entry; WHO (COG-006) does not say whether entry is at the facility or the district.

short: The national reporting system reached all 91 public health facilities (WHO, 2025), but it is not known where their reports are entered.
gaps: No row says where DHIS2 reports are keyed: the 99% (2024), the 69 facilities (August 2024) and the 91 structures or 100% (2025) are shares of all public facilities the system reaches or that report through it, not of primary clinics entering their own data, and the only keying level on record is the region, for the predecessor GESIS in July 2021. Tiers are read from 'all public structures' only; the plan row is dated July 2021, outside the 36 months, and the 2025 extension is dated to the year, so it cannot be placed inside the twelve months.

short: The national reporting system operates in every public health facility (February 2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held: the two terms of reference say DHIS2 is in production in all structures, which is deployment, and CPV-004 says the source does not state who keys the reports. Nothing on the HMIS is dated after 2024-02, and no plan or finance is stated for it.

short: 84% of all health facilities entered their own data in June 2025; it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
gaps: Inside the 36 months no row gives a current plan naming the system or a domestic budget line: the only plan rows date from 2020 (DJI-016, DJI-020) and the only finance row is UNFPA's support for one integration (DJI-008). The 84% is of all facilities with no numerator or denominator, the tier row names the primary care level only, and nothing is dated inside the twelve months to the as-at (the 69% to 84% rise ends 2025-06-30); the 2020 tier rows (DJI-017 T2;T3, DJI-022 none) disagree with the 2025 one, which stands.

short: The ministry began training staff on the national reporting system in December 2023, starting with a team of 20; nothing yet shows it in use.
gaps: The two rows held (DZA-008, DZA-009) are governance only: a first team of 20 trained on DHIS2 in December 2023 and a digital health strategy still in draft in November 2023. Nothing says which tiers report through it, where data is keyed or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; finance is not stated, and there is no dated statement that reporting has no digital entry.

short: Births and deaths are entered at district level into the national health information system (2025); routine clinic reporting is not shown.
gaps: The one row describes the flow of birth and death notifications only, from health offices on paper to electronic processing at district level; nothing shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system, and the latest year the source cites is 2011. No tier, clinic share, governance or twelve-month fact is held.

short: Reports are entered at zone and sub-zone offices (2024); no primary clinic is shown entering its own.
gaps: No row states that any primary clinic enters its own reports, and no share or count of clinics is held outside the excluded source (ERI-001). The district reach disagrees across rows: all zobas by 2019 (ERI-011), 44% of districts in 2022 (ERI-008), zones and sub-zones in 2024 (ERI-004), and no row says in so many words that sub-zones key the clinics' paper forms. The tiers fact is from 2021; finance is not stated; the plan row (ERI-006, HSSDP III 2022-2026) is dated 2021-10, outside the 36 months, so plan:current is not carried; nothing is dated inside the twelve months.

short: Hospitals and health centres enter their own reports into the national system (2024); it is not known whether health posts do.
gaps: No share of primary clinics entering their own reports is established: the 95% figures count all health facilities using DHIS2 (ETH-021, published 2023, no counts) or 'eligible' institutions implementing it (ETH-031, over 4,000, including district hospitals and district offices), while ETH-022 and ETH-023 from the same 2023 study say health posts have no HMIS of their own and report on paper through their health centre, and systems.csv counts 17,903 health posts. These disagree, and nothing dated after 2020 says health posts enter their own data. ETH-024 is a 2025 annual completeness figure, not a dated event; eCHIS is said to synchronise with DHIS2 by one undated regional page and not to be linked by two later sources, so community integrated is not set.

short: The national system was launched in December 2024, with 122 data managers trained across 51 health departments; clinics are not shown entering their own reports.
gaps: No source gives a share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports, and none names the tiers: GAB-027 says only that DHIS2 integrates all functional public facilities, and that the clinics report on paper is stated only by the excluded source (GAB-003). Completeness figures disagree (60% to 85% at the December 2024 launch in GAB-029; 35% in 2024 and 40% in 2025 in GAB-011), and the 2025 rise carries a year only, so no dated event is placed inside the twelve months.

short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national system, and some community health posts enter their own (2024); how many is not published.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of primary clinics entering their own reports: the ministry's 2022 plan says only that 'most facilities' enter into DHIMS2 themselves, and the one survey (86 purposively chosen CHPS zones in six Northern Region districts, March 2024) both reports entry at CHPS level (GHA-009) and CHPS staff without logins or computers whose paper goes to the district (GHA-010). The only clinics figure is none of 16 facilities in 2016-2017, a sample that does not carry the country. The plan is the Ghana Health Service's digital health policy and strategy for 2023-2027 (GHA-043), which names DHIMS II and covers the as-at; the ministry's 2022-2025 plan has ended. Nothing on DHIMS2 is dated inside the twelve months.

short: All levels reported into the national system in early 2026, with clinics' paper reports entered at district offices.
gaps: No share or count of health centres or health posts entering their own reports is published; the 100% completeness of Q1 2026 (GIN-009) is data transmitted, not facility entry. The sources disagree on where data is keyed: the 2021 yearbook and a 2022 project statement have some health-centre heads entering in DHIS2 (GIN-034, GIN-037), while the newer rows have paper tools keyed at the district (GIN-025) and rural centres reporting on paper (GIN-024); GIN-025 is dated only to its published year.

short: Clinics reported on paper, and regional health offices entered the figures into the national reporting system, in 2024.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and nothing is held for the twelve months to the as-at. The tiers facts disagree: the policy (GMB-016, the newest) puts DHIS2 at the regional directorates and the centre only, GMB-013 shows one secondary hospital feeding it automatically in a pilot, and GMB-025 and GMB-027 say every tier's data reaches DHIS2 without saying where it is keyed; no finance fact falls inside the 36 months.

short: Health centres' paper reports were entered into the national system at 11 health directorates (June 2023); how many clinics enter their own is not published.
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after June 2023. Clinics: the 2022 yearbook (GNB-010) counts reports, not centres keying their own, and disagrees with the 2018 pilot value (GNB-020), whose tablet entry from health areas has no later fact and no number of sites. Tiers: the 2019 presentation (GNB-017) gave T1;T2;T3 and the 2022 yearbook row speaks of health centres only. Governance: the plan fact (GNB-013, PENSIS 2022-2026) is dated 2022 and is carried because its period covers the as-at; finance is donor on the one row inside the 36 months (GNB-022, the Global Fund through UNDP), and no domestic line is stated. The October 2026 support agreement (GNB-021) is for data quality, dashboards and patient-tracking tools, not a change in where reports are entered.

short: The national reporting system was piloted in two districts, Baney and Añisok, in 2025; a planned national expansion in 2026 is not confirmed.
gaps: No source names the tiers or counts the facilities entering data in the Baney and Añisok pilot, and nothing dated after November 2025 shows the national expansion foreseen for 2026 under way. The digitised facts disagree by place: facility or district-office entry in the two pilot districts (GNQ-017, GNQ-018), paper sheets transcribed to spreadsheets by ministry staff elsewhere (GNQ-015); the plan held in the window (PNDS 2021-2025, GNQ-013) is not said to name DHIS2, and the domestic budget facts are of 2019 and 2020, outside the 36 months.

short: Facilities across the country enter their reports online into the national system (2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so themselves.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics keying their own reports is held: KEN-041's 94% (2019/20) is a reporting rate, not facility entry, and KEN-035 names no tier individually. KEN-036 (2024, entry at the facility) and KEN-024 (2016, district and national) disagree on where data is digitised; the newer stands. Finance rows are 2015 and 2016, outside the 36 months; the plan row KEN-038 is dated 2023-07, two months before the window opens, and is kept because the plan runs to June 2027. No dated event falls in the twelve months.

short: All facilities report monthly into the national system (2024), with district and county clerks entering the figures from paper forms (2022).
gaps: No national figure for clinics entering their own reports: LBR-037 finds none in 48 facilities of three counties (2022), which does not carry the country, and LBR-043 and LBR-046 publish none. Nothing on where data is keyed is dated after 2022-07; the only last-twelve-months row (LBR-008) is dated to the year 2025 and cannot be placed inside the window, and the CBIS is described as a DHIS2 sub-system while its integration with DHIS2 is still planned, so no community flag is set.

short: The national system was rolled out to 465 primary care facilities and 51 hospitals in 2023; how many clinics enter their own reports is unknown.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 465 primary facilities (LBY-025) are where DHIS2 was rolled out, with no denominator, and WHO says consistent facility reporting remains a challenge (LBY-016). Sources name hospitals and PHC facilities, not levels; a 2021 assessment (LBY-007) called DHIS2 a pilot not in routine use, against the ministry's 2021 report tabulated from DHIS2 entries (LBY-032); the 2024-2025 operational plan is not shown to run to the as-at, and the donor finance fact is dated 2023.

short: 231 facilities report HIV figures into the national system (2025); clinics entering their own data is shown only in four pilot districts, up to 2017.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of primary clinics entering their own reports: facility entry is evidenced only for the four pilot districts to June 2017 (LSO-024) and for reports automated from the eRegister (LSO-017), and how facilities without it enter theirs is not stated. Tiers and clinics have nothing dated since 2017; finance inside the 36 months is not stated (the donor rows are 2015 and 2022); the 2025 advance (LSO-003) is dated to the year only and the same year carries falling reporting rates (LSO-018, LSO-019), so no twelve-month flag is set. LSO-004 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: A national reporting system was working in every public health centre by December 2019; no figure shows how many centres enter their own reports.
gaps: The coverage facts disagree: at December 2019 the SMIPF-SC was operational in every public health centre (MAR-013, MAR-014), worded as 100% with no numerator or denominator, while the newer March 2023 baseline has an integrated system deployed at hospitals and only begun in primary centres, with no count (MAR-026, MAR-027). No source says the health centres key their own reports (MAR-015), and nothing on coverage is dated after March 2023; finance:domestic (MAR-024, 2022) falls outside the 36 months.

short: Health centres in all 114 districts report into the national system, with district offices entering their paper forms (2023).
gaps: No count or share of basic health centres keying their own monthly report: the electronic RMA is available in 10 pilot districts of 114 with no facility count (MDG-017), and the 2025 deployment of electronic registers and tablets (MDG-002) gives no count either. The donor-finance statements (MDG-014, MDG-027) predate the 36-month window, and the WHO facts on completeness, modernisation and CHRD data quality (MDG-001 to MDG-003, which disagree on direction) are dated only to 2025, so none can be placed inside the twelve months.

short: Community and referral health centres and hospitals had routine data in the national system in 2019; how many clinics enter their own is not known.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 98% of September 2019 (MLI-016) is DHIS2 deployed in community health centres, with no numerator, denominator or statement of who keys, and facility entry is evidenced only for four sub-districts of Mopti in 2018 and, uncounted, for SNISI terminals at CSCom and CSRéf. Tiers and coverage are not dated since 2019; finance is not stated inside 36 months (the donor-dependence fact is of February 2021) and no dated event falls in the last twelve months; MLI-005 and MLI-006 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: District health offices entered facilities' monthly paper forms into the national system in 2019; nothing more recent is held.
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after 2019, and nothing says which tiers use SIS-MA or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; the clinics value rests on a 2016-17 sample of 16 facilities in four districts. MOZ-016 (2019, a literature review citing a 2013 paper) gives facility-level recording and disagrees with MOZ-019 and MOZ-013, which describe district keying from paper; it names no facility entering data and is not followed. Finance is held only from 2019 (MOZ-017, donor), outside the 36 months, and no event is dated inside the twelve months.

short: District offices enter health posts' paper reports into the national system (2023); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 92 per cent in MRT-016 is report coverage, with no numerator or denominator, and MRT-011's 'deployed nationally' (2025) is not facility entry and disagrees with MRT-017 (2023), which has DHIS2 piloted and not scaled up. Health posts report on paper, only two hospitals are integrated (MRT-010), and the one event in the twelve months is a training workshop for district focal points (MRT-008).

short: In January 2022 the national system was used only at regional and national level, with entry by clinics still planned; nothing more recent is held.
gaps: No row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, and nothing on the HMIS is dated after January 2022: whether the decentralisation to district and primary level then planned has happened is not established, nor whether DHIS2 carries routine patients-treated reporting rather than surveillance and immunisation aggregates. Governance facts are all from January 2022, outside the 36 months, and the plan they name ran 2020-2024, so no governance value is held; the only digitised facts are a 2018 rating of no electronic aggregate entry at district level (MUS-027) and a 2020 statement on Rodrigues alone (MUS-035).

short: District offices enter paper reports from 1,266 facilities into the national system (2023); how many health centres enter their own is not published.
gaps: No count or share of health centres entering their own reports is published (MWI-040, MWI-050, MWI-061). The sources disagree on where data is keyed: the ministry's 2023 report says DHIS2 Mobile allows direct entry by all health centres (MWI-048, MWI-049), while the later-dated study (MWI-043) and the August 2023 survey (MWI-022) find paper forms keyed at the district office. The only plan on record is a 2019 finding with no period (MWI-039), so no plan is held at the as-at.

short: Clinics report on paper, and district officers enter their monthly forms into the national reporting system (2026 study).
gaps: No row sets the tiers in use, and no share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: the minister's count of over 90 clinics reached by data collection (NAM-020, May 2025) has no total and names no system, and the newer NAM-004 and NAM-005 (March 2026) have district entry from paper and clinics on paper, so the newer stands; NAM-015 (2025-09) has four of 20 respondents saying primary facilities upload some data. On the plan, the managers' statement that no health information systems policy exists (NAM-008, published March 2026) stands against the National Digital Health Policy 2026-2036 launched in February 2026 (NAM-018), whose period covers the as-at. The only event inside the twelve months is that launch (NAM-019), not a change in where reports are entered.

short: A 2023 ministry guide has health centres enter their monthly reports into the national system; no figure shows how many do.
gaps: No count or share of integrated health centres keying their own reports into DHIS2 is held: the 2023 guide prescribes facility entry and does not measure it, and the only figures are 2021 completeness and timeliness of reports transmitted. Nothing on finance is dated inside the 36 months (the donor financing row is 2019), nothing is dated inside the last twelve months, and no community system is shown exchanging data with the SNIS.

short: 91.5% of all health facilities reported into the national system in June 2025, with local government offices entering the figures from paper.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: NGA-028 (2025-06, valued facility) only encourages states to deploy devices for direct reporting and gives no count, and it disagrees with NGA-030, NGA-032 and NGA-033, which have paper forms keyed at the LGA office. The only clinic figure is 0 of 16 sampled facilities in 2016-2017 (NGA-025), which does not carry the country; no dated event is held for the last twelve months, and the domestic commitment in NGA-010 is not broken down to DHIS2.

short: Every health facility enters its own reports (audit to 2023); it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
gaps: No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months to the as-at: the only plan fact (RWA-020, plan:none) is dated 2021 and no row states finance, so the cap holds. The 100% is a rollout statement with no numerator, resting on 13 facility visits; whether the 1,250 health posts key their own reports is not established, the newest tier fact (RWA-024, 2024-06) names no T4, and reporting completeness is held only undated (RWA-011). Nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: Local health offices entered facilities' reports into the system in 144 of 189 localities in 2020; nothing since April 2023 shows where data is entered.
gaps: Every coverage fact dates from 2018 to 2022, before the conflict of April 2023; nothing since says where data is keyed, which localities still enter it or whether any facility enters its own, and the ministry's 56 per cent reporting coverage at the end of 2025 has no numerator or denominator. On tiers the 2021 figure for selected hospitals (SDN-023) disagrees with the 2020 and 2018 statements that DHIS2 was not in hospitals or facilities (SDN-027, SDN-035), and it does not say the hospitals key their own reports.

short: The national system is used at every level, with figures entered from the district upwards (2021); how many clinics enter their own is unknown.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and no coverage fact is dated after 2021. The facts disagree on where data is keyed: the ministry's 2021 plan (SEN-025, newest) runs DHIS2 from the districts up, while SEN-057 (2021) and SEN-020 (2018, four districts) describe entry at health posts. The regressing fact inside the twelve months (SEN-035) carries its document's date, not an event's, and the finance in SEN-036 was not yet approved.

short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national reporting system (2020 procedure, 2023 assessment).
gaps: No fact says a primary clinic keys its own reports: the 96% of SLE-010, SLE-032 and SLE-039 is DHIS2 deployed in facilities surveyed, with tracker applications joined in, and SLE-041 puts T3 and T4 under that deployment only. The January 2023 facts disagree on where data is digitised, at the facility in hospitals (SLE-042) and at the district (SLE-043); the district stands for the clinics, on the April 2020 procedure (SLE-048), and nothing dated since says whether the 2020 plan to move entry to community health centres took effect. Finance is held only for 2022, outside the 36 months, and no event is held for the last twelve months.

short: District offices enter paper reports into the national system (2022), and 111 primary facilities report digitally (2025); their share of all clinics is unknown.
gaps: No denominator of primary clinics is held for the 111 facilities that produce their DHIS2 reports digitally, and no share of facilities entering their own data is published; the 2026 commentary calls implementation uneven without a figure. The facts disagree on where data is digitised (district from paper in September 2022, facility in the 111 RAAD sites by 2025) and on tiers (T4 primary health care units counted in 2022, no facility-type breakdown in the 2023 bulletin). The August 2025 UNICEF and HISP agreement falls outside the twelve months, so advancing rests on one NGO training in Bosaso in February 2026; the plan is read as current on the 2022-2026 and 2022-2027 periods, the five-year strategy's own period not being given.

short: The ministry says 30% of all health facilities entered their own reports into the national system in 2025, without giving the numbers behind it.
gaps: The 30% is a share of all health facilities with no numerator or denominator, and the tier of the facilities keying their own reports is not stated; the two 2025 facts on where data is keyed disagree (SSD-015 facility, SSD-016 centralised at a level it does not name), and SSD-011 says the PHCC and PHCU vouchers are configured, not where they are keyed. On the plan, the HSSP 2023-2027 targets for DHIS2 (SSD-019) stand against a February 2025 self-assessment that lists an HIS strategic plan as still to be established (SSD-008).

short: The national reporting system was introduced in all districts in 2024-2025; who uses it and where reports are entered is not yet known.
gaps: No admissible row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, where the data is keyed or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; the only rows on those three aspects (STP-001, STP-002) come from the excluded source. Finance is held only as donor at September 2022 (STP-012), outside the 36 months, and the advancing event (STP-006) is dated to the 2024-2025 biennium with no month, so it falls in the twelve months only on the year-end reading.

short: Hospitals and maternity units record births and deaths digitally (2022), and the national reporting system was introduced in 2024; clinic reporting is not yet shown.
gaps: No row says which tiers enter routine aggregate reports, where clinics' reports are keyed, or how many primary clinics enter their own; the one digitised fact (2022) is hospitals and maternities recording births and deaths, and it disagrees with the 2019 profile's statement of no electronic aggregation (SWZ-032). No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months; the only plan fact is from 2019.

short: The 2022 health plan describes data capture as mainly paper-based, with digital work stalled; nothing shows digital reporting, so no stage is set.
gaps: No row gives the tiers reporting digitally or the primary clinics entering their own reports. The one coverage fact (SYC-004) says capture is primarily paper-based and the eHIS work begun in 2020 has stalled, which is neither a dated statement of no digital entry at any level nor a contracted rollout; it carries the plan's published year, not a date of its own. The ministry's ownership is dated 2022, outside the 36 months, and finance is not stated.

short: District offices enter health centres' monthly paper reports into the national system (Gavi audit, 2024); how many centres enter their own is not known.
gaps: No source gives a share or count of health centres entering their own reports; the only facility-level statement of none is one district in 2018 (TCD-027), which does not carry the country. Tiers disagree: TCD-019 (2023) has hospitals on DHIS2 with a slow migration, TCD-028 (2018) has health centres and district hospitals reporting on paper. Finance is donor on a 2021 fact outside the 36 months, so not stated inside the window; plan:current rests on PNDS 4 2022-2030 (TCD-022), since the 2025 strategy does not name the system.

short: 96.5% of all health facilities entered complete reports into the national system in 2021, the ministry says; there is no separate figure for primary clinics.
gaps: The share is for 2021, printed as a rate without its counts, covers all facilities and not primary clinics alone, and nothing newer is held; WHO's annual report gives 89.2% for the same year (TGO-021). TGO-026 records no coordinated digital health strategy across the systems while the PNDS monitoring plan 2023-2027 (TGO-031) names DHIS2 and runs past the as-at; no domestic budget line is stated, and community entry into DHIS2 is a procedure requirement, not an observed count.

short: Nothing held describes routine health reporting; a national health information system was named in 2021 with no sign of use, so no stage is set.
gaps: The country has no evidence row on HMIS: nothing is held on routine aggregate reporting, at any tier. systems.csv names a 'système d'information sanitaire national unifié' being put in place in 2021, unclassified and with no fact behind it.

short: Clinics report on paper, and council offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2024).

gaps: No fact dated by the as-at names a station entering reports or dockets in a system: the electronic docket system was announced in December 2025 as coming soon (ZWE-009), and the 2021 pilot study for rural stations (ZWE-015) gives no station and no record, so the newer fact stands for stations. Which record the system will hold is not established, the last statement on how records are made dates from 2021, and no finance is stated inside the 36 months. The Warren Park proof of concept (ZWE-001 to ZWE-005) is dated 8 October 2026, after the as-at, and sets nothing; ZWE-006 to ZWE-008 are from the excluded source.

short: Since 2023 births are entered digitally at offices in Luanda and three other cities; most offices use paper, and the digital count is not known.
gaps: No source counts the offices registering in RCI: it is in Luanda's registries (39 units in the province) and one post each in Huambo, Benguela and Lubango, against at least 255 units nationally (more than 300 on the 2024 decree), and the majority of units are on paper, with SIRC offices holding records locally. Deaths in a digital system are not described, no source says the outage reported on 5 May 2026 has ended, the two maternity-post openings in the twelve months (AGO-009, AGO-010) read advancing but do not say the record is digital, and RCI's dependence on a private developer (AGO-031) sits against the ministry's ownership.

short: Digital civil registration runs in about twelve pilot communes in 2026, most acts still on paper; how the pilot record is made is not known.
gaps: No source says the system is past its pilot, how the digital record is made in the pilot communes or where it is held: thirteen communes 'have' a biometric registration system (count 13, no total given; 12 in the ministry's own July 2026 presentation), which is not thirteen registering. Births and deaths entered digitally rest on one commune, Rumonge, in 2024; no plan with a period covering the as-at is on record (the only plan fact is a 2017 table entry), and no domestic budget line is stated for the civil platform.

short: Births are registered digitally at maternity desks in ten pilot health facilities since August 2025; how other local offices make the record is not known.
gaps: The one-stop desk has not left its ten facilities: the pilot ended in February 2026 and a consolidation phase runs in the same ten, with generalisation three to four months late. How ANIP's communal units and the civil-status centres make the record is not described: the 2021 law and the May 2026 playbook say every birth and death is registered in the national register, without saying where or by what means the entry is made, so deaths and offices beyond the ten are not established. No plan with a period is on record, and finance disagrees: donor support on the newest fact (BEN-009), self-financing with no budget line named in the playbook (BEN-043).

short: Birth-entry software was deployed in 170 civil registration centres in 2025; the total number of centres, and how many register in it, is not known.
gaps: The 170 centres of 2025 (BFA-006) are centres the software was deployed in, with no total of centres and no statement that they register in it; the budget review (BFA-039) gives 0 main centres producing acts digitally at 30 June 2025, which disagrees. Deaths rest only on a training session in one commune (BFA-003), and no fact says where the VENEEM record is held; whether 2025's 170 includes 2024's 116 is not stated.

short: A national system registered births and deaths in 2024; how many of the 35 district offices enter records in it is not known.
gaps: No fact says how many of the 35 district offices and 17 on-site points enter records in the BDRS (BWA-004), and the newest fact on how the record is made (BWA-003) does not say in terms that it is keyed at the office; the only count is 13 hospitals in 2015 (BWA-023). No plan is held inside 36 months: the 2021-2026 CRVS plan is only scheduled in a 2019 document (BWA-017). The kiosk closures (BWA-010) are undated, and BWA-015 reports an online service built but not live.

short: A civil registration application was still being developed in July 2026 and offices register on paper; the number of pilot offices is not known.
gaps: No office is shown entering a birth or death digitally: the registrar's own statement of 18 July 2026 is an all-paper system with the software still under development (CAF-005, CAF-006). The pilot of December 2024 (CAF-016) gives no count of offices and does not say what was piloted, and it sits beside the July 2026 statements that the software is not yet deployed. The PNEC is given no period and is not said to name the software; the newest events fact is from 2017.

short: In March 2026 the registrar said 98 per cent of civil status centres were computerised and connected; whether any registers births digitally is not known.
gaps: No admissible fact says a centre registers a birth in Citiweb: every offices figure is of centres equipped, computerised or deployed (98% on 2 March 2026 with no numerator or denominator; all centres at end 2025; 699 centres on 11 August 2026 with no total), and the World Bank said on 18 September 2025 that the registry is still on paper. How the record is made is not established: the only connected fact is from the excluded essay and the only local one is the 2019 decree's permission, which places nothing; the SNECI is given no period and is not said to name the software, and the 2026 finance law's domestic line names no system.

short: In September 2026, 60 of 432 principal civil status centres were digitised, 13.9 per cent; the share of all local offices is not known.
gaps: The share is 60 of 432 principal centres on BUNEC's figures of 14 September 2026, which the source calls a pilot phase; the 2,400 or so secondary centres are outside the denominator and are planned to stay on paper, so the share of all local offices is lower and not published. Last twelve months disagree: EcoMatin says the rate has hardly moved since April 2022, while dated events show first digital birth acts at Limbe I on 7 January 2026 and in the East Region by August 2026. No national budget line is stated; one commune's maintenance line does not carry the country.

short: In August 2025 one commune of the capital was piloting digital civil registration; whether any birth or death has been registered digitally is not known.
gaps: No fact says an event has been registered digitally: the Masina pilot's births and deaths are stated as its aim (18 August 2025), and its own dates and results are not given. Last twelve months rests on a UNDP tender of 25 April 2026 for the design of digital tools; the one other dated event, a North Kivu sector office out of paper registers in July 2026, is one office and does not carry the country. No count of offices newer than the 979 of March 2019.

short: A civil registration system was built and validated by September 2026 but no office uses it; whether older urban systems still run is not known.
gaps: No office is said to use SIFEC at 22 September 2026, and the B;D rows (COG-004, 006, 008, 018, 022) give the scope of a system not yet deployed, so events is read as none. Older facts disagree with the newest: electronic records kept locally in some Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire centres (COG-032, 2021; COG-036 and 2 of Brazzaville's 10 offices digitised, COG-037, 2020) against a system called manual in 2026 (COG-017) and 2024 (COG-043); nothing since 2021 says whether those urban systems still run. Finance: COG-015 (not stated, for SIFEC's deployment) is newer than the donor rows COG-030 and COG-025. The roadmap (COG-034, COG-039) is from 2020-21 with no period given, so no plan is held.

short: In 2026 offices register on paper while a digital system is studied and costed; when its three-centre pilot starts is not known.
gaps: No system exists yet: the eCRVS is proposed by a study validated on 25 March 2026, and its three-centre pilot (Moroni, Mutsamudu, Fomboni) has not started. The costed plan (COM-004) and the 2024 strategic plan (COM-022) are given no period; plan:current rests on COM-004 saying the country holds it in August 2026. The newest paper statements say 'largely' paper (COM-001, COM-021), not paper only; the only flat statement is from 2017 (COM-034). COM-016 (ANEC decree not adopted, March 2026) is the one no-change event against nine advancing.

short: In 2017 offices in all 22 municipalities entered births and deaths digitally, in urban centres only; whether records reach the national register is not known.
gaps: No report of practice says the entry made at the conservatória is held in the national register: CPV-008 (2017) does not say where the record is held, CPV-001 (2025) does not say the entry is made at the office, and CPV-003 and CPV-005 are what the law prescribes, which places nothing. The office share is 22 of 22 municipalities from a profile compiled to November 2017, with stations in urban centres only; nothing newer gives a share or a rural share. No governance fact is dated inside the 36 months and no event inside the twelve.

short: Nine civil-status sites in Djibouti-Ville have entered births and deaths digitally since 2011, as stated in 2024; digital entry outside the capital is not known.
gaps: The newest dated facts (ESCWA's 2025 survey, DJI-003 to DJI-005, held as an ingest note and not as the passage) say local offices hold no electronic records of births or deaths, which disagrees with the city's 2024 account of SIGEC; no row dated to the as-at says any office outside Djibouti-Ville enters digitally, none gives a national count of offices, and SIGEC is not said to be held in a national register. No plan is stated, nothing is held for the last twelve months, and no row shows a birth registration issuing the NNI in practice, so identity integrated is not set; no admissible row names rural offices, so rural gap is not set.

short: Births are registered in a national digital register across 1,541 communes, a 2019 count; the share of local offices entering digitally is not known.
gaps: The 1,541 commune databases are a 2019 count given with no total of local offices (communes and their administrative annexes), and the newest offices fact (DZA-012, 2025) gives no count or share entering digitally and finds paper persisting. The facts valued connected (DZA-002, DZA-008) do not say the entry is made at the commune office when the event is registered; the law keeps paper registers and sends a digitised copy. Nothing is held for the last twelve months and no rural figure is given.

short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at 4,571 health offices, as stated in 2026; the share of all offices is not known.
gaps: No total of health offices is given against the 4,571 (2017 and 2026) or the 4,666 linked (2025), and the two counts differ; 'full nationwide automation' is a statement of offices automated, not a share registering. Egypt's undated answers to the WHO EMRO questionnaire (published 2025) disagree: paper at registration points, electronic entry at the governorate centre, and health-office entry only as a pilot in selected governorates. Finance is not stated in the newest fact, though a 2024 page credits the State budget; no rural share is published.

short: Births and deaths were handwritten at local offices and entered in regional electronic registers one level up in 2017; current practice is not known.
gaps: The record-making facts date from 2015 and 2017 and nothing since describes how a birth is entered; the newest events fact (ERI-006, 2025-11) names only the computerised death certificate and does not say where it is entered, so B rests on ERI-009. No count of offices doing digital entry, no owner and no finance are stated, the 2024-2028 plan is not said to name a digital system, and nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: Digital registration of births and deaths is in pilot, in Addis Ababa and 1,300 of 19,202 kebeles in 2025; use beyond pilots is not known.
gaps: No fact shows a system past its pilot outside Addis Ababa: the July 2026 presentation does not say which rollout phase had been reached, and the offices facts disagree (pilot in ETH-003, ETH-011, ETH-016 and ETH-023; count:50 in ETH-013, an announced start in the capital with no total; count:100 in ETH-027, capital only, 2018). The connected facts do not say the entry is made at the office, and ETH-015 (2025-07) calls registration mainly paper-based. Finance is not stated for the eCRVS, and the only finance fact in the window is donor support to ME-CRVS (ETH-025, 2023). Whether the birth feeds the Fayda number is stated only as a possibility in systems.csv, so identity integrated is not set.

short: No office registered births or deaths digitally in May 2026; a system is being prepared with funding to 2028; its first offices are not known.
gaps: No office registers digitally and no pilot office is named; the CNEC is not yet in operation and the legal framework for digital registration was rated not implemented at 31 May 2026. The count held is of departments (0 of an unstated total), not offices. No domestic budget line is stated. GAB-001 and GAB-002 are dated after the as-at and set nothing.

short: Births were registered digitally at two Accra registry centres in 2024; how many offices do so, and how the record is made, is not known.
gaps: No national count or share of offices entering births digitally: the only count is two registry centres in one Accra municipal district (2024-10), a floor. How a birth record is made is not stated in any row; the one `made` fact is for deaths, paper forms scanned at the national office (2022), and nothing says entry is made at the office and held in the national register. Deaths rest on the platform's name and on scanned forms. No dated event in the twelve months. The plan for 2025-2030 was still to be approved in July 2025 and does not name the platform; the budget line names no system. The identity link was launched in March 2024 and systems.csv records it suspended after a fault and re-tested in August 2026. GHA-002 to GHA-004 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: Commune offices made digital birth certificates in September 2026, when a paper shortage halted printing; how many offices do so is not known.
gaps: No count or share of offices: one commune's officer says all communes, with no count beside it, so it is not read as 100 per cent. `made` disagrees: GIN-002 (2026-09-02) has the commune system depending on a data centre, while GIN-010 (2026-03-03) has Conakry's 13 communes supplied with paper registers for 2026 and GIN-018 (2026-02) has registrars still on paper in parallel; the newest stands, but its words do not say the entry is made at the office. Offices disagree too: pilot in ten communes (GIN-013, 2023-08) against not-published (GIN-003), the newest standing. The fact does not say whether the digital birth certificate is the registration of the birth or the issue of a secure copy, nor whether the system is E-RENEC. No plan is stated. Owner disagrees in the window: vendor (2026-09), partner (2026-04), ministry in law (2025-04, 2023-10). GIN-017 (July 2025) falls outside the twelve months. GIN-006 to GIN-009 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: Births are registered on a central digital system, with 79 local offices holding digital registers in 2025; the total number of offices is not known.
gaps: The 79 civil registration offices have no total against them, so the count is a floor; the same 2025 source also yields 258 health facility points (GMB-016) and, in its deck, no figure for how many points enter records (GMB-035). Both `connected` facts say the source does not state in terms that the record is keyed at the registration point at the moment of registration. No death module is in operation. GMB-021 and GMB-022 (a policy published 2024-02) call CRVS paper-based with no event registered digitally; the newer facts stand. No domestic budget line is stated and the World Bank operation ended in August 2025. The CRVS strategy was still to be finalised in the 2025 diagnostic; plan:current rests on the 2023-2028 strategy and the 2021-2030 health policy. Backlog capture rests on one systems.csv line from the 2024 policy, undated in its text. GMB-036 (April 2025) falls outside the twelve months. GMB-006 and GMB-007 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: One Bissau office registers births and deaths digitally in 2026, and health posts in three regions register births; the share of offices is not known.
gaps: No count of offices or posts entering digitally against the country's own total (13 conservatórias and 80 posts in GNB-030; 55 offices and 20 health sites in GNB-035): the one counted office, Santa Luzia, is in Bissau, and the posts in Tombali and Quinara (GNB-011, GNB-012) are uncounted, on a platform the source does not name or say is connected. GNB-007 calls Santa Luzia the first fully digital office in 2026 while GNB-011 and GNB-015 report digital registration from 2025; no dated source in the evidence other than the excluded essay says rural offices are outside the system, so rural gap is not set.

short: A digital pilot registers births in Malabo only, since 2018, and the seven regional offices use paper in 2024; its present state is not known.
gaps: Nothing on the state of SIREC is dated after the World Bank diagnostic of 2024, and nothing falls in the twelve months to the as-at. No fact says how the pilot itself makes the record, or how many offices in Malabo use it. Every owner fact is dated 2017 or 2018, outside the 36 months, so owner is left empty; the plan held (GNQ-010, 2022-2026) is the statistics strategy and its passages do not say what the civil registry system does.

short: More than 270,000 births were registered digitally from hospitals in two months of 2026; how many offices or hospitals use the system is not known.
gaps: No fact counts the hospitals or offices using the e-birth registry of 2026; the newest offices fact, KEN-014 for 2023, reports no office entering digitally, and predates the system. KEN-002 has parents entering the data in the hospital and does not say the entry is made at a registration office; systems.csv carries the same system as an e-notification processed at the civil registration office. Deaths are not on the system. No plan is held for the period: KEN-023's ran 2018 to 2022.

short: County teams registered births online in 2024, with deaths added to the platform; how many of the 58 centres enter them is not known.
gaps: No source counts the centres entering births on the DHIS2 platform: the two newest office facts (LBR-012, LBR-015; 15 counties, 58 centres) publish no number, and the only count is 14 centres in 2015 with no total (LBR-032), which does not say the centres make the digital entry. LBR-017 (May 2024) says County Service Center services remain mostly paper, against LBR-010's county teams registering online; the 2024 policy (LBR-006) gives no period and is not said to name the platform; nothing is dated inside the twelve months, the last event being 2024 (LBR-013).

short: All civil registration offices were automated and linked to one database, the health ministry said in 2022; whether events are entered there is not known.
gaps: LBY-006 and LBY-007 say all offices are fully automated and electronically linked to one database; they do not say a birth or death is entered at the office when it is registered, so the share is read as equipped, not registering. The figure is the health ministry's, undated and published 2022, with two counts of service offices (400 and 380) and no rural share; no plan or finance is stated in the 36 months.

short: Births were registered digitally at 30 health-facility stations in three districts in 2026; the total number of local offices is not known.
gaps: No total of local registration offices is given, so both counts are floors: 30 SMS-supported stations in three districts (LSO-002, 2026) and 15 enrolment centres online to the central server (LSO-023, 2022), which are different systems and are not reconciled. How the SMS platform's record is made and where it is held is not stated, LSO-014 does not name the register, and LSO-022 says the centres allow for birth registration without saying the entry is made there; nationwide scale-up is an action for 2026-2027 and deaths are not shown entered at any local office.

short: Offices enter births and deaths in a ministry system said in 2024 to reach every office; the share of offices registering digitally is not known.
gaps: No share of offices registering is held: 'all offices' (MAR-013, 2024-10-29) is the ministry's word with no count beside it, and the 59 of 97 (MAR-004, 2026-01-30) is over a programme's participating municipalities for a system whose function the report does not state. Later facts disagree with the 2024 account: in October 2025 communes were short of the paper registers called essential for registering births (MAR-009) and access to the national platform was still to be opened (MAR-010); MAR-014 gives the central connected platform as what the programme is to provide. The plan (MAR-016) carries no period, the domestic finance fact is from 2014 and outside the window, and the identifier at birth is held only as what Law 36-21 provides.

short: Communes register births digitally, 336 of them in December 2025; the share of all communes this represents is not known.
gaps: The 336 communes (MDG-007, December 2025) are given as 40% of the project's target, not as a share of all communes, so the count is a floor; the newer fact (MDG-005, 2026-03-02) says only 'several communes'. MDG-009 does not say in terms where the record is held, and the offline module was only in demonstration. No plan is held inside the 36 months (the plan:none fact is from 2016), no domestic budget line is held, and PRODIGY's financing closed on 30 June 2026 with no later fact on what funds the system; the software's future after OpenCRVS stops was unsettled. No digital death registration is reported.

short: Births were registered on paper in July 2026 and a digital platform had ten pilot areas named; whether any has started is not known.
gaps: No office is shown entering an event digitally: the platform of MLI-007 and MLI-008 (2024-12-16) is approved with ten pilot areas identified and not said to have started, so B;D is what it is to cover, not what is registered. Nothing dated inside the twelve months speaks to movement. The strategy held is for 2018-2022 (MLI-014), a period ended before the as-at, so no current plan is held; finance:domestic rests on ANSAEC's endowment in law with no amount or budget line (MLI-005), beside donor support (MLI-009). The 2016 City-web fact (MLI-011) names no office and its link to the NINA is not confirmed at the as-at, so identity integrated is not set.

short: Births are entered directly at district offices and all 68 conservatories were digitised by 2025; the share of local offices entering digitally is not known.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of local offices making the digital entry: the registrar's 68 of 68 conservatories are 'digitised' (equipped) and leave out the posts below them, and the newest fact (MOZ-006, 2026-08-28) publishes no figure. Facts disagree on deaths (MOZ-004 and MOZ-033 give B and D; MOZ-016, 2025, names death registration as a challenge) and on how the record is made (MOZ-034 has district offices entering directly; MOZ-035 has 534 community points on paper forms keyed at the district office, which no fact calls rural, so no rural gap is flagged); MOZ-001 does not say the new maternity posts enter digitally.

short: By law births are recorded centrally at citizen reception centres, 153 of 168 equipped in 2021; whether centres enter births digitally is not known.
gaps: No fact outside the law says a centre enters a birth digitally when it is declared: events and how the record is made rest on Laws 2011-003 and 2025-011 (MRT-003, MRT-004, MRT-009, MRT-010), which place nothing, and the one other fact on either is from the excluded essay. The office figure is centres equipped against a planned network of 168, from August 2021, with nothing newer; no governance fact falls inside the 36 months (the newest is 2022-11) and nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: Births and deaths are registered online at computerised civil status offices, 35 listed in 2019; the share of all offices is not known.
gaps: No share of offices making the digital entry: the Registrar's 35 computerised offices (2019) is a count with no denominator, the deck does not say in terms that every office enters records, and the newest fact (MUS-007, 2025-09-06) gives no count; the only share, 32 of 47 in 2012, is from the excluded essay. The plan held (MUS-018) is the Strategic Directions for 2023/2024, a period ended before the as-at, and both last-twelve-months facts (MUS-005 of 2025-09-06, MUS-020 of 2024) fall before the window opens on 2025-09-30.

short: Births and deaths were entered digitally at 87 local service points in five districts in 2025; the share of local offices is not known.
gaps: No share of local offices is published: 87 Traditional Authority service points in five of 28 districts stand against 277 TAs and 138 Sub-TAs listed for expansion, and the 58 health facilities (2025) and 142 health centres (plan) carry no total. MWI-039 (owner:partner, CDC and EGPAF maintaining the CRVS system) disagrees with the newer owner:ministry rows; MWI-033 records CDC funding expected to stop in March 2026, an expectation and not an event; the NRB's own 2025 pages (MWI-049, MWI-052) describe a paper NR8 procedure and name no digital system; the rural gap rests on MWI-044 (2024), which gives no figure. MWI-001 to MWI-003 are dated after the as-at and MWI-007 to MWI-011 are from an excluded source: none was used.

short: Local offices enter births and deaths in the national register, as reported in 2024; the share of offices doing so is not known.
gaps: No share of offices registering digitally stands at the as-at. The newest office fact, NAM-014 (statistics agency, April 2024), says some remote offices lack computers or internet and gives no count; it disagrees with NAM-025 (September 2023, share:100%), which says all 62 local centres are connected to the NPRS, is not the registrar's or the statistics office's statement, lists offices that sum to 59, and is contradicted in the same document by NAM-026. No plan covering the as-at is held: the CRVS plan ran 2015/16 to 2020/21 and no later one is named. finance:domestic rests on NAM-020, dated at the window's first day. The rural gap carries no figure, and backlog capture rests on systems.csv (a running project to capture old death records, 2023). NAM-001 to NAM-003 and NAM-040 to NAM-044 are from excluded sources and were not used.

short: The digital register ran in 101 of 266 communes in December 2024, a share of communes; digital death registration outside Niamey is not known.
gaps: The share is 100 communes of 266 principal centres (NER-033, an undated page given the year 2026), a share of communes read as offices; it agrees with the statistics office's 101 of 266 in production (NER-042, December 2024) and the government's 102 communes with no total (NER-027, April 2026). It disagrees with NER-014 (UNICEF, 10 August 2026), 68 per cent of communes computerised with no numerator or denominator, which is a share equipped and would also place at stage 3. Deaths are evidenced digitally only for the five Niamey arrondissements in 2023 (NER-046); NER-040 and NER-041 (December 2024) call registration paper based, against the connected rows. The 13,939 village and health-facility declaration centres are not said to be computerised, and the rural gap rests on NER-049 (2023), with no figure. Most last-twelve-month rows are works announced, not delivered, and the commune count did not rise between May 2025 (103) and April 2026 (102). NER-031 and NER-032 are from an excluded source and were not used.

short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at ward and local government offices from July 2026; the share of local offices doing so is not known.
gaps: No share of local offices entering on VitalReg is established: 3,372 wards activated (NGA-027, 18 July 2026) has no total of wards, and the 4,011 registration centres (NGA-014, NGA-023, NGA-035) are a count of centres whose facts say they do not state how many enter on the platform; the two counts disagree and are of different units. NGA-027 also says only 15 states have ward registrars while other rows say all 36 states and the FCT, and paper fallback where the network fails is reported (NGA-001, NGA-040, NGA-041). Finance is donor or not stated; no domestic budget line is held.

short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at all categories of registration office in 2025, the statistics office says; the rural share is not known.
gaps: The 100 per cent is the statistics institute's statement that NCI-CRVS is fully operational at all categories of registration office in 2025, beside the totals of 416 sectors and 2,148 cells; it gives no count of offices using the system and no rural share. The two newer offices rows (RWA-002, RWA-006) publish no figure, and RWA-006 has cell secretaries still in training, in a text dated by publication that reads as older. Within the twelve months RWA-024 reports timely death registration falling from 96.3% to 89.9% in 2025, against rising completeness (RWA-023); the launches in RWA-009 and RWA-016 carry publication dates only.

short: Births are registered in a national electronic registry, with one local office named in 2026; how many offices enter records, and where, is not known.
gaps: How the record is made rests on a 2023 account of the pre-war centralised electronic registry (SDN-010), which does not say at which desk the birth entry is keyed; nothing since the war began says how or where the record is made. The only office figure is one office issuing an electronic birth certificate on 17 May 2026 (SDN-005), with no total and no statement of how the underlying record is made. The twelve months disagree: closures in Darfur and Khartoum (SDN-001, SDN-002) are undated and carry publication dates, while the dated events are two Gezira offices reopening (SDN-004, SDN-006), so no flag is set. No governance fact falls inside the 36 months; deaths are not evidenced.

short: In 2026 civil-status centres register births in one national system, with 77% of 629 centres digitised; the share entering data is not known.
gaps: No fact gives a share or count of centres registering events in the LGEC: every figure (77% of 629 in September 2026, 471 and 437 of 629 earlier) is centres digitised, deployed or covered, and SEN-015 itself says equipped centres are not the same as centres entering data. Deaths are held in the system (SEN-034) but no fact says they are entered at the office at registration; no rural share is given, only regional deployment rates (SEN-032); the total of centres is 629 in 2026 and 689 in SEN-054; finance:domestic rests on an unnotified 2026 agency budget (SEN-013) and an unquantified 'substantial public funding' (SEN-056), beside EU finance to June 2026 (SEN-042).

short: In 2023 births were entered digitally at the registration authority's hospital centres and sent to a central registry; the number of offices is not known.
gaps: No count or share of offices doing the digital entry is published: the 48 (SLE-018, September 2024) are health facilities given laptops and modems, none said to be registering, so the count is a floor of equipped sites at best. The only offices named as entering births digitally are in Freetown (Ola During Hospital, 34 Military Hospital), the fact for entry at the office dates from March 2023, and death registration with the application is not described. No plan with a period covering the as-at is held (the 2017 roadmap gives none), no domestic budget line appears in an evidence row inside 36 months, and nothing is dated inside the last twelve months.

short: By January 2026 local administrations in 30 districts registered births digitally into one central database; the total of districts or offices is not known.
gaps: The 30 districts (SOM-008) carry no total of districts or offices, so the count is a floor and no share can be read; it is a count of districts read as offices, on an undated page whose January 2026 date is a proxy. Deaths are enabled on the platform (SOM-010) but only births are counted as registered (SOM-007). SOM-012 calls the 19 districts of August 2025 a pilot where SOM-009 calls the system production-level; the newer stands. No dated event falls inside the last twelve months: the launch of 10 August 2025 (SOM-016) is outside it, and the move from 19 to 30 districts has no date of its own. The roadmap (SOM-014) gives no period and no domestic budget line is stated.

short: A digital civil registration system was announced in July 2026 and no birth is registered digitally; its design and start date are not known.
gaps: Preparation rests on announcements of July 2026 and an undated memorandum of understanding: no design, procurement, pilot office or start date for a digital system is described, and whether the Juba birth-registration pilot (SSD-023, SSD-024) is digital is not stated. On the plan, SSD-022 (December 2025) says a costed CRVS plan was adopted but gives it no period, against SSD-013 (July 2026), which describes recommendations and no plan in force.

short: Births are entered directly in the national database at maternities, as of 2026; the share of local offices doing so is not known.
gaps: No share or count of local offices entering records is published: the registrar says all maternities, with no number and nothing on the other offices (STP-006), and the World Bank gives 11 centres and seven maternity posts without saying how many enter records in SIGA (STP-020). Deaths are named for the system (STP-009, STP-010, STP-013) but no fact says where they are entered, and the newest fact (STP-004) names births only. No finance fact falls inside the 36 months; the plan named in STP-015 has no period and STP-022 says there is none for civil registration.

short: Births and deaths were entered in the national register at 14 service centres in 2022; the total number of offices is not known.
gaps: The 14 service centres registering in the National Population Register in 2022 (SWZ-012) come with no total of offices, so the count is a floor; the software 'installed in all centres' is equipped, not registering, and the AfDB and COMESA 'all offices' (SWZ-016) carries no count. The only total held is in a governance row of December 2024 (SWZ-015: 15 service centres including headquarters, and 5 hospital points), a different year and not read against the count. The World Bank's June 2026 appraisal disagrees with the older facts: well over 90% of civil records on paper (SWZ-001) and electronic civil registry services not active (SWZ-004). No rural share and no office figure within two years.

short: A computerised record of vital events was kept beside the manual register in 2018; where it is entered is not known.

short: Births were registered digitally at 97 hospital registry points in 2025; the total of local offices is not known.

TCD-017's words do not say the entry is made at the office, which only TCD-044 says, of six hospitals in 2023. No admitted source states a rural gap, and the N'Djamena register digitisation is planned, not under way.

short: A digital birth registration platform was piloted at one town hall in 2024; whether other offices register on it is not known.
gaps: No admitted fact says how the record is made on the digital birth registration platform or on Kadodo: the only `made` row, TGO-015, is 2018 data and speaks of paper exchange between offices, not of the entry. The 16 Savanes communes (TGO-010) are centres digitised and trained to use the platform, not said to register on it, and no total is given beside them (TGO-001 mentions 117 communes). Owner rests only on the 2009 law (TGO-007), outside the 36-month window, so it is not carried; the 2024 roadmap (TGO-006) gives no period.

short: Registrars enter births and deaths into the national database after the paper register, all offices connected in 2020; how many register is not known.

Nothing on how the record is made or on offices is dated after 2020; no plan whose period includes the as-at and no finance fact inside the 36 months is held (TUN-009 and TUN-020 plans ended by 2021, TUN-019 donor finance is 2021).

The 57% is centres RITA counts as active, the inactive ones lacking the phone that uploads, not a stated count of centres entering digitally; TZA-017 says some centres' registrations are keyed by district officers, and the newer TZA-011 (12,025 points, 2025) gives no total and no number entering digitally. Inside the 36 months no domestic finance fact is held (TZA-025 is 2018) and the plan in TZA-014 ran to 2025/26, ending June 2026; the only event inside the twelve months is Zanzibar's (TZA-005), the mainland's being October 2024.

short: District offices enter births and deaths into the central register, in most districts in 2020; how many offices do so is not known.

The sources disagree on how the record is made: NIRA's January 2019 questionnaire has paper at the lowest centres keyed at regional level (UGA-040), the 2020 brief has entry at district offices into the central register (UGA-033). UGA-002 (July 2026) reports a new births module on NSIS with no offices and no date of going live, and UGA-009 does not say the current plan names a registration system; no dated event falls inside the twelve months.

short: Births are registered online at 242 equipped health facilities, as of March 2026; the share of local offices registering digitally is not known.

Deaths have no digital registration on record; the twelve-month advance (ZAF-046) carries no figure, while e-Birth missed its 2025/26 targets (ZAF-047, ZAF-051); no dated source says in terms that rural offices are outside the system, so rural gap is not set. ZAF-001 and ZAF-002 are dated after the as-at and ZAF-006 to ZAF-008 are from an excluded source; none was used.

short: Births are registered in a national system deployed in eleven districts in 2026; how many local offices enter records themselves is not known.

The facts also disagree on where entry is made: ZMB-015 and ZMB-017 have paper forms keyed at provincial or national headquarters, while ZMB-002 has one district office registering through INRIS in September 2026, which does not carry the country. Deaths are reported registered in INRIS (ZMB-010, ZMB-016), though the Minister names death certificates only as intended (ZMB-007). The cost of the exercise is stated without a source of funds (ZMB-009), an older fact naming donors (ZMB-022). Nothing dated inside the twelve months says the system advanced or regressed nationally. ZMB-004 and ZMB-005 are from an excluded source.

short: Births are entered digitally at computerised offices; at least 93 of 282 offices were computerised in 2026, and how many register digitally is not known.
gaps: The Registrar General's department counts all 10 provincial and 63 district offices and more than 20 of 209 sub-offices as computerised (ZWE-010), at least 93 of 282, and does not say what a computerised office does: that is a share equipped, about 33 per cent, not a share registering. ZWE-020 says entry is made in real time at the office but not where the record is held or whether offices are online to a national register; some sub-offices are still not computerised (ZWE-003, ZWE-007). Deaths have no digital entry on record. Finance for the computerisation is donor in every fact that names it, while the 2026 Appropriation Act funds the civil registration programme whole from domestic revenue with no system line (ZWE-014). The February 2026 shortage of certificate paper (ZWE-013) is a regress in issuing certificates, not in digital entry, and is not flagged. ZWE-012 is from an excluded source.

short: Schools answered a twice-yearly school count questionnaire in 2021/22; whether any primary school keeps a per-pupil record is not known, so no stage is set.

short: It is not known whether primary schools keep pupil records on paper or in a system, so no stage is set.

short: A December 2025 brief describes paper-based school data collection; whether primary schools keep a per-pupil record is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: SEN-001 and SEN-002 are from the source the study excludes and set nothing. The one admissible row, SEN-003 (2025-12, dated by publication), speaks of paper-based education data collection and isolated digital files at school and sub-national level generally: it does not name learner records, primary schools or paper only. No admissible fact on any system holding a record per learner; systems.csv holds census-class, noted and unclassified systems (PLANETE 3.0 and EDUSTAT undescribed or future).

short: In 2022-23 a rollout gave 300 primary schools tablets to enter each pupil's daily attendance; how many do so is not known.
gaps: The 300 is a count of primary schools in the Wi De Ya rollout phase, not of schools entering data, and no total of primary schools is given with it; nothing is dated after 2023 on its use, and the planned rollouts to 1,500 and 4,000 schools are not confirmed. The newest schools fact, SLE-001 (2026-04-07), is a different system, the Unique Learner ID, still to be piloted with no school yet using it. short: A daily per-pupil attendance app was on trial in 42 schools in Puntland State in May 2022; what has happened since is not known.
gaps: SOM-001 is from the source the study excludes and sets nothing. The newest admissible fact is May 2022: the Digital Attendance Application on trial in 42 schools, in Puntland State only, their level not stated (read as primary), with state-wide collection not in place. Nothing is dated inside the 36 months to the as-at, so governance and the last twelve months are empty, and whether the planned roll-out to about sixty schools happened is not established. Nothing admissible on a learner-record system outside Puntland.

short: Teachers reported each absent pupil by text message in 2024; the share of primary schools doing so is not known.
gaps: No share of primary schools entering attendance: SSD-008's 6,650 is schools of all levels that reported at least once, with no primary total and no clear denominator (5,915 open schools holding enrolment, 10,364 ever identified), and the same page shows 1,321 messages from 3 phones in the last month. The newer SSD-002 and SSD-003 (2026-03-24) say school-level collection relies heavily on paper, which disagrees with SSD-007's routine SMS entry. No plan and no ministry owner is held, and nothing dated inside the twelve months says advancing or regressing; SSD-001 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: Schools sent data to the ministry's school-management system in 2023; whether primary schools keep a per-pupil record is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: evidence.csv holds no row for the country. systems.csv names SIGE several times, as a census where it is classified and otherwise unclassified, with a relaunch in a first group of schools still at tender in January 2025; none of it is an evidence row.

short: A per-pupil record has covered all 976 primary and secondary schools since March 2024; how many primary schools enter attendance or results is not known.

SWZ-004 does not say how often a school enters the learner record, and SWZ-018 and SWZ-019 put SEMIS, the app that takes attendance, still at its pilot with roll-out to come. No plan is held, no dated event inside the twelve months says advancing or regressing, and SWZ-001 to SWZ-003 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: The ministry trained school leadership teams on its pupil record platform in 2026; whether any school enters attendance or results is not known.
gaps: No row reports a school entering attendance or results: SYC-003 is the helpdesk's instruction for taking attendance, not a report that schools do it, and SYC-001 is training of school leadership teams on Mahé only.
